overview: A June 1941 memo on an undisclosed Japanese Embassy approach, and a July telegram (plus Navy paraphrase) reporting unconfirmed claims Japan suspended merchant shipping to Thailand, recalled vessels, and canceled trade orders.

people.name: Hugh Gladney Grant
people.role: U.S. Minister to Thailand; signer of the Bangkok telegram

people.name: Arthur H. McCollum
people.role: Commander; recipient of information conveyed by the Department of State

people.name: Cabot Coville
people.role: Official in the Department of State's Division of Far Eastern Affairs and apparent drafter of the June 4 memorandum

subfiles.title: Telegram from Bangkok on reported suspension of Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: Reports rumors that Japan had suspended merchant shipping between Japan and Thailand, recalled vessels, and restricted commercial orders.
subfiles.summary: Grant relays unconfirmed Bangkok reports that Japan ordered merchant ships suspended to Thailand, recalled vessels at sea, and that firms were rejecting and canceling orders.

subfiles.title: Confidential paraphrase of Bangkok Telegram No. 251
subfiles.about: Provides a confidential paraphrase of the report concerning the alleged suspension and recall of Japanese merchant vessels.
subfiles.summary: Confidential paraphrase repeats unconfirmed reports of Japan halting shipping to Thailand and recalling vessels, circulated to the Navy in July 1941.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning notification of Commander McCollum
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (apparently drafted by Cabot Coville)
subfiles.about: Records that Commander McCollum was informed of an approach made to the Department by the counselor of the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Memo notes McCollum was told of a June 1941 Japanese Embassy approach to State, though the substantive attachment explaining it is missing.

interest: Shows rumored 1941 Japanese shipping suspension with Thailand, amid State-Navy coordination before the Pacific crisis.
